title: Understanding Media: Spotting Different Viewpoints
text: Explore how different media share information, how viewpoints shape messages, and how to decide if sources are trustworthy.
cdi_links: 3.S.01 Understanding different media sources and evaluating reliability

title: Introduction
text: In this lesson, you will explore
bullets: Different types of media and information sources
How viewpoints influence what we see or hear
How to judge if information is trustworthy

title: Success Criteria
bullets: I can name different types of media and information sources
I can explain what a viewpoint is and why it matters
I can identify bias and judge whether a source is trustworthy

title: Key Words
bullets: Media – Ways we get information, like TV, social media, or newspapers
Viewpoint – Someone’s opinion or perspective on a topic
Bias – When information is unfair, one-sided, or misleading

title: Starter Questions
text: Where did you get your news yesterday?
Have you ever seen two sources report the same event differently?

title: Different Media Sources
bullets: TV and radio news
Newspapers and magazines
Social media platforms like TikTok or Instagram
Blogs, podcasts, and YouTube channels
Websites like Wikipedia
Each source may present facts differently depending on audience or purpose

title: Spotting Viewpoints and Bias
bullets: A viewpoint is someone’s opinion or perspective
Bias happens when information is presented unfairly, favouring one side
Does the source show all sides of a story?
Are opinions presented as facts?
Who made the information, and why?
Understanding this helps you think critically about what you read or watch

title: Activity
text: Explore different media sources, evaluate viewpoints and bias, and decide whether sources are trustworthy. Include discussion, sorting, and reflection exercises as appropriate.

title: Key Takeaways
text: Different sources may present information differently
Checking the source is key to judging trustworthiness
